headline: Government considers a defence spending freeze
description: Reinmetall’s CEO says he’s already feeling chilly and has told workers to wear thicker socks.

quip.text: Defence budgets and I go way back. Mostly back. Ouch, that hurts.

headline: Defence budget frozen. Soldiers told to carpool in tanks
description: With the heating budget frozen too, soldiers huddle inside their tanks to keep warm.

headline: Government discovers that carpooling in tanks still costs money
description: In a breakthrough for the cabinet, ministers discover that tanks still burn fuel with all the seats taken. The heat of the idea thaws the defence budget.

headline: Candidate promises free pizza for every voter
description: Polls surge. Economists ask where the ingredients for all that pizza will come from. The candidate says, “A farm, probably.”

quip.text: Free pizza? I already own most of the farms. Do you have any?

headline: Pizza Act passes: one pizza per citizen per week
description: Down to Earth Farms reports a sudden and delicious spike in demand for wheat, tomatoes and cheese.

headline: Euro leaders spend six hours debating the font on new banknotes
description: Comic Sans lost by a single vote. Currency traders describe the mood as "typographically uncertain".

headline: Parliament expresses interest in "yeeting stuff into outer space"
description: The bill specifies neither a destination nor a payload. Space yeeters (aerospace lobbyists) are weeping with joy.

quip.text: I looked at MOO years ago. It’s going to the moon.

headline: Cheese war breaks out between the Netherlands and Germany
description: Germany’s chancellor proposes a cheese wall to stop cheese tourism. Farmers fear export chaos while Switzerland declares itself neutral but fondue-ready.

headline: The cheese war is over!
description: According to insiders, negotiators reached a good deal. Exports resume immediately.

headline: World peace treaty fails over seating arrangements
description: The evening peaked when China’s leader threatened to nuke Russia over who got to sit at the head of the table. Defence stocks jumped.

headline: EU Parliament member seen wiping his nose with a Swiss franc bill
description: Traders question what a franc is worth if it doubles as a tissue. The Swiss franc slips and the euro rises.

headline: Two nations declare war over a disputed parking spot
description: Both armies are "extremely serious" and both parked in the same place. Defence and energy stocks surge. Gold pays the price of fear.

quip.text: Wars come, wars go. Defence stocks stay. Like my back pain.

headline: Parking spot war ends in confusion
description: Turns out it was a no-parking zone. Defence stocks crumble.

headline: Navy of 40,000 pigeons blocks the Strait of Hormuz
description: Every tanker captain in the strait has had their hat stolen by a pigeon. The captains are furious. Crude prices lift off.

headline: Pigeons unionise and the Strait of Hormuz reopens
description: Local politicians reluctantly agree to supply every pigeon in the strait with bread on Fridays. Tankers can sail again.

headline: Superpowers try to settle border dispute by chess, but one side cheats
description: Observers noticed one leader’s chair vibrating before every move. When the loser called an emergency summit, weapons makers and gold hoarders perked up.

headline: Embargo declared on socks; "we can hear the sandals"
description: Footwear diplomacy escalates. Defence contractors report "unusually motivated" procurement.

headline: Frost hits coffee belt and baristas declare a national emergency
description: Bean prices jump. Baristas lose patience with customers asking if the frost means iced coffee is cheaper now.

quip.text: Honey, did you see the news about coffee? Apparently it comes out iced now!

headline: Oil found under a US national park
description: The park ranger is drafting a strongly worded letter. The oil company is already millions of barrels deep.

headline: Oil-exporting countries hold meeting rumoured to be a very long brunch
description: Nobody knows what was decided, but everyone left two kilos heavier.

quip.text: Brunch decisions are the best decisions. I once bought a boat at brunch.

headline: Oil-exporting countries cut production by "a lot"
description: The exact figures are still keeping traders in suspense while the executives sleep off brunch. Crude prices rise.

headline: Billionaire buys gold to feel something
description: His therapist suggested a hobby. He appears to have misunderstood the assignment.

headline: Billionaire buys a tonne of gold for his new hobby and accidentally tanks the price
description: “I didn’t mean that kind of hobby. Have you tried pottery?” asks his therapist. He puts the whole tonne back on the market in one go.

headline: Phone makers discover silver is shiny and add "Shiny Mode" to flagship phones
description: Demand surges even though the silver is hidden inside the phone. “It’s there, trust us,” says one manufacturer. “Shinier means better.”

headline: Drought sends farmers looking for supernatural solutions
description: Crop yields collapse as farmers turn to ancient rituals and rain dances. Farm shares and coffee prices rise while growers wait for an answer.

headline: Cows sign pledge to stop burping by 2030
description: Down to Earth Farms has to buy expensive anti-burp feed for the entire herd. Shareholders want to know who let the cows sign.

headline: Silver mine in Peru floods and miners turn it into a pool
description: Output halts while the pool is “enjoyed responsibly”, says the CEO from the shallow end, still wearing a hard hat. Silver supply tightens.

headline: New flu "Mondayitis" spreads. Offices shut for "mild cases"
description: Symptoms include staring at the wall and requesting coffee. Pharma and coffee demand rise.

headline: Placebo Pharma to reveal results of "it works if you believe" trial
description: Analysts believe the results will be announced shortly.

quip.text: I believe. I believe very hard. Mostly in free samples.

headline: Regulators approve belief-based medicine
description: The pill works for everyone who is told it works. Placebo Pharma stock lifts off.

headline: Rumour: Placebo Pharma's miracle pill may be "just sugar"
description: The company calls the rumour “baseless, but sweet”. Influencers call it the next candy trend while doctors panic.

headline: Placebo Pharma’s miracle pill is fake
description: “But it’s very effective sugar,” says Placebo Pharma. Regulators are not amused. Shares crash as customers feel tricked.

headline: BMUU recalls 400,000 cars: blinker fluid shortage
description: Drivers report that they "never knew there was blinker fluid, and now we are all worried".

headline: BMUU launches blinker subscription at $19.99 a month
description: Customers may now rent the right to turn left. Analysts call it genius and evil. Real fans ask what indicating even is.

quip.text: I never knew you had to indicate in a BMUU.

headline: HypeLoop CEO tweets nothing but a pair of eyes for three hours
description: Millions speculate on what he is looking at. The HypeLoop hype is real. And perhaps looping.

headline: HypeLoop CEO’s long-awaited reveal is a terrible mixtape
description: Investors feel betrayed. The CEO follows up with a broken heart and a fire emoji.

headline: Moonshot’s next rocket may land in a giant bouncy castle
description: Moonshot wants to catch the booster and fly it again. Space fans are cautiously optimistic. The engineers ask who has to stand next to the castle.

quip.text: Bouncy castles are fun, and fun is money.

headline: Moonshot buys the world’s biggest bouncy castle
description: The delivery takes up the entire landing pad. Even the analysts are starting to think it might work.

headline: Moonshot makes history by catching a rocket in a bouncy castle
description: The booster bounces once and stays put. Even the engineers look surprised. Moonshot investors are suddenly a lot richer.

headline: Down to Earth Farms caught labelling rocks as "organic"
description: Customers say the rocks were "firm, but not very juicy". Shares plunge. The company promises to "regroup, replant and rebrand".

quip.text: The taste was all right, but I lost two teeth.

headline: ClosedAI promises a model that understands printer errors
description: IT support workers are thrilled. They’re projected to own at least 20% of ClosedAI by the end of the year.

headline: Users report that the model has itself become the printer error
description: Support tickets are answered with "PC LOAD LETTER". The share price is not coping.

headline: Macrohard update removes the Update button
description: Users now have no way to update the update. The company says this is "a feature".

headline: AlphaBett: "We are now a bank, a dentist, and a cloud"
description: B for banking, C for cloud and D for dentistry. AlphaBett is three letters closer to owning the whole alphabet. Analysts can’t decide whether it’s brilliant or a cry for help.

headline: Global chip shortage
description: Carmakers and tech giants report that “the little squares are mostly gone”. A prominent CEO demands that people with spare chips at home donate them to big tech.

headline: Parliament bans AI from writing parliament speeches
description: The AI speeches were "too coherent". AI stocks wobble. The vote passes unanimously.

headline: Rumour: AlphaBett quantum chip is "simultaneously working and not working"
description: The lab says it is "probably both". Nobody will open the box.

headline: Observed: the AlphaBett quantum chip works. Probably.
description: The scientists opened the box. The cat is "inconclusively fine". AlphaBett soars.

headline: Data centre cooled by one very old fan catches fire
description: Cloud customers are asked to "please stop uploading memes". AI and tech stocks tumble.

headline: “Going outside maxxing” takes off and social media usage plummets
description: Parents are delighted. HypeLoop executives are trying to work out how to put ads on trees.

headline: NotRugpullCoin team posts "We're definitely staying" from a luxury yacht
description: The photos show enough cocktails and models to make good decisions unlikely. NotRugpullCoin rallies anyway because investors think the party looks pretty rad.

quip.text: I tripled my money in NRC. They’d never rug-pull us. It’s the most stable coin.

headline: NotRugpullCoin plummets overnight
description: Roughly a luxury yacht and a very large party’s worth of money has vanished from the liquidity pool. The founders have stopped posting.

headline: Celebrity dog appears in crypto ad
description: The dog does not appear to know what crypto is. Investors do not care. WoofCoin goes to the moon.

headline: Celebrity dog denies knowing what crypto is
description: “Woof,” says the dog in a statement. WoofCoin reverses violently. Cat fans are thrilled.

headline: Bitcorn banned in country with no internet
description: Regulators insist the ban is "extremely effective". Crypto traders panic anyway.

headline: Bitcorn ETF approved after a single elevator pitch by a 15-year-old
description: Wall Street calls Bitcorn a mature, trustworthy investment. Crypto Twitter has been posting moon pictures for hours. Prices jump.

headline: Man finds four million Bitcorn on an old laptop
description: Fears of a sell-off hit the market. The man says he can’t remember the password.

headline: Bitcorn "halving" party: investors stock up in advance
description: Supply shrinks in a few days. Someone brought half a cake.

headline: Halving complete: nobody understands it, everyone cheers
description: The party ended with "half the guests and double the hype". Bitcorn surges.

headline: Tiny nation replaces gold standard with the banana standard
description: Gold traders feel "peeled". Banana-adjacent farm stocks celebrate.

headline: Meme cat gets its own IPO
description: Several brokers report accidentally buying HYPE because of the hype. WoofCoin surges too after investors mistake the dog for a cat.

headline: Parliament votes to cancel Mondays
description: Coffee sellers shudder as one fifth of the demand disappears at once.

headline: Mondays reinstated after Tuesday inherits all of Monday’s work
description: By Tuesday morning, everyone had two days of work and one day to do it. Coffee orders doubled before Parliament could vote Monday back in.

headline: Switzerland adds a 25th hour to catch up on punctuality
description: Swiss clocks now chime "later, but exactly". The franc is a safe bet.

headline: Unprecedented demand for good goat cheese. Even the central bank accepts it as collateral
description: The rush for goat cheese pushes food prices up, and the euro dips as traders worry about inflation. Farmers suspect they are “sitting on a gold mine, but with holes”.

headline: Llama escapes from a Silicon Valley zoo
description: Big Tech announces a major LLaMA breakthrough. AI stocks surge before anyone asks why the demo is eating hay.

headline: Study finds every meeting could have been an email
description: The economy saves 4 billion hours overnight. Productivity software vendors celebrate quietly, by email.

headline: Central bank announces an announcement about interest rates
description: The announcement will be made "soon", "ish" and "in a tone". Traders position themselves nervously.

quip.text: Rate cuts are like free pizza. Everybody smiles and has more money left for dessert.

headline: Rates cut: markets confused but excited
description: Nobody knows why, but cheap money makes stocks sprint. Gold approves. The euro does not. The bartenders’ union says it wasn’t involved.

headline: European Central Bank raises interest rates by group-chat poll
description: The poll was 5 to 4 with two abstentions and one thumbs-up emoji. Traders doubt the bank has a plan and move their money from euros into Swiss francs.

headline: Overworked Bank of Japan staff caught taking a group nap
description: The rate desk sleeps through its own briefing. With no update coming, traders sell the yen.

headline: Bank of Japan fixes the yen before the coffee gets cold
description: An emergency meeting is called. Coffee is served by the pot. The bank announces a plan to steady the yen, and it works. Coffee prices tick up too.

headline: Market panic: someone coughed during the opening bell
description: Traders mistake a cough at the opening bell for the start of an outbreak. They dump stocks and crypto and buy gold, Swiss francs and yen.

headline: Market recovers: it was just allergies
description: A spokesperson blames pollen. Traders buy back stocks and crypto and sell the gold, Swiss francs and yen they picked up in the panic.

headline: Tech and engineering market mood declared “immaculate vibes”
description: A survey finds 100% of traders have forgotten what red looks like after seeing green every day. Stocks and crypto rise as traders sell gold to buy more shares.

headline: Swiss National Bank finds 4 tons of gold in grandmother's couch
description: The grandmother wants "finder's fees and tea". The extra supply pushes gold down. The Swiss franc rises.

headline: D. Trump wants to blow up Mount Rushmore. “I will make the mountain great again.”
description: The US leader calls the monument "a renovation opportunity". Reinmetall investors hear the word explosives and stop listening to the rest of the speech.

headline: Chinese hackers leak BMUU technology ahead of its unveiling
description: The leaked blueprint shows two wheels and a large marketing budget. BMUU calls the design “revolutionary” and asks everyone to wait for the official launch.

headline: BMUU unveils two-wheeled car that is "definitely not a bike"
description: Executives demonstrate the optional pedal package and insist the handlebar is a steering innovation. Investors are overjoyed. BMUU opens orders for a market debut in four days.

quip.text: I’ll pick up so many girls with this two-wheeled car.

headline: BMUU two-wheeled car misses sales targets. Customers buy bikes
description: The market debut sells three units, two to the marketing department. Investors are surprised that a bicycle with a car payment is a difficult pitch. BMUU shares crash as the board promises a relaunch.

headline: Melon Musk tweets: "NRC is going to the moon"
description: NotRugpullCoin traders buy before checking whether Melon means the coin, a rocket or his new nightclub. The tweet contains no further details and twelve rocket emojis.

headline: NotRugpullCoin creator "Asuspicious Per Son" reportedly sells everything
description: Investors are shocked that the extremely reliable Asuspicious Per Son would sell everything. NotRugpullCoin crashes.

quip.text: Oh man, that was my guy. I trusted him with my whole heart.

headline: ClosedAI promises a huge leap in AI-driven robots at upcoming convention
description: The invitation says the demonstration will "flip your expectations". ClosedAI investors start buying ahead of the convention in three days.

headline: ClosedAI robot manages only three backflips; investors wanted four
description: The robot completes three perfect backflips. It announces that it’s out of power, then falls flat on its face and is damaged beyond repair. The audience calls it a technological disappointment.

headline: Russia’s V. Putin reportedly sends containers of vodka to AlphaBett headquarters
description: A tipsy executive assures reporters that AlphaBett is on steady footing, then leans on the podium. Investors worry the next product roadmap may be just as shaky.

quip.text: I wish I was working at AlphaBett right now.

headline: Macrohard unveils Windows Classic. Investors buy the nostalgic feeling
description: The launch promises the comfort of an older operating system with the confidence of a modern price tag. Macrohard shares rise while reviewers wait three days for their copies to finish installing.

headline: Windows Classic turns out to be the 1998 operating system
description: Reviewers find no new features, the original bugs and the same security problems. Macrohard insists that “unchanged” is a premium nostalgia feature. Investors disagree.

headline: Cheese trade tensions rise between the Netherlands and Germany
description: Border guards demand documentation for every slice. Both governments describe the situation as "mature but escalating". Reinmetall receives inquiries about armoured cheese transport.

headline: Local grandma declares total war on upstairs party-makers
description: After a third sleepless night, she announces a defence budget and a strict no-bass doctrine. Reinmetall investors know from experience what happens when you underestimate an angry grandma.

headline: Postal services say AlphaBett navigation routes every van to ice cream shops
description: Parcel deliveries are late, but driver satisfaction has never been higher. Major postal customers threaten to cancel their navigation contracts. AlphaBett shares slide.

headline: Rumour: ClosedAI develops model exceptionally good at identifying squirrels
description: The model distinguishes squirrels from slightly different squirrels with astonishing accuracy. ClosedAI investors struggle to identify a customer and begin questioning what they have funded.

headline: Squirrels carrying incurable disease escape laboratory. UN offers tracking bounty
description: The UN urgently needs a company that can find the escaped squirrels. ClosedAI announces that its suspiciously specific model is ready.

headline: Macrohard CEO spotted bench-pressing 200 kg at local gym
description: Analysts upgrade Macrohard from "solid fundamentals" to "absolutely massive fundamentals". Investors pile in after a photo proves the CEO can, literally, lift the company.

headline: Football star kicks ball into space: "Just kick something really hard"
description: The striker says rockets are an unnecessary waste of money. “You just need to kick it really hard.” Investors question Moonshot Aerospace’s entire business model.

headline: Moonshot unveils pet drone for rainy days
description: Dogs get their daily “air walk” without bringing muddy paws back into the house. Pet owners are already asking where to buy one.

headline: BMUU CEO takes submarine car to the Titanic to prove its capabilities
description: The CEO calls deep-sea pressure "a branding challenge" and promises a live demonstration. Investors cheer BMUU's expansion into a market with almost no traffic.

headline: BMUU CEO reportedly missing after submarine car implodes near the Titanic wreck
description: Investigators say the vehicle's depth rating was listed as "optimistic". BMUU shares collapse as the board suspends the submarine-car programme and announces a safety overhaul.

headline: All major US supermarket chains accept NotRugpullCoin as payment
description: Retailers describe the coin as "extremely safe" and "trustworthy", citing its name as their main due-diligence document. NotRugpullCoin surges as shoppers prepare to pay for groceries with reassurance.

headline: Billionaire spends entire fortune on silver because it looks pretty
description: Asked about diversification, the billionaire orders a second shade of silver. The purchase sends silver prices sharply higher as interior designers rush to buy what’s left.

headline: Middle Eastern leader Warpin vows to bomb coffee plantations in three days
description: After one bitter espresso, Warpin declares that “the beans must answer for this”. Reinmetall and coffee traders watch the three-day ultimatum with bated breath.

headline: Fifty coffee plantations hit overnight after Warpin's bitter-coffee ultimatum
description: Reinmetall shares rise on fresh orders. Coffee buyers cancel contracts over fears of further attacks and disrupted shipments.

headline: Leaked memo: Swiss minister will swap half the franc reserves for cheese
description: An insider forwards a memo scheduling the conversion in three days. The minister's entire written justification is "I love cheese". Traders wonder how liquid a wheel of fondue can be.

headline: AlphaBett CEO caught having an affair with a Chinese spy
description: The board calls an emergency meeting. Investors dump AlphaBett shares before anyone can take minutes.

headline: AlphaBett CEO spotted in an extremely cool leather jacket
description: Investors take one look at the jacket and decide he’s got this. AlphaBett shares go to the moon.
